title: Behavior specifications using ground-truth evaluation repositories
description:
Build a deterministic evaluation system for scanner quality across components, data flows, PII signals, and future data-item output.

The system uses two evaluation tiers:

1. Fast committed fixtures for CI. These prove scorer and adapter behavior and provide regression coverage.
2. A versioned benchmark of pinned third-party repository scopes. Humans review every scanner-relevant declaration or finding within each annotated scope so unmatched scanner output can be counted as false positives and missed ground truth can be counted as false negatives.

Metrics are reported separately and never averaged:
- Recall: matched positive ground truth divided by all evaluable positive ground truth.
- Label accuracy: correctly labelled matches divided by matched positives.
- Correct-label recall: correctly labelled matches divided by all evaluable positives.
- Precision: true positives divided by all scanner findings inside exhaustively annotated scopes.
- Negative-case pass rate: explicitly annotated negative cases left clean. This is a regression guardrail, not a substitute for precision.
- Unread or unsupported cases are reported separately using exact per-file scan coverage.

Each output layer has an adapter that produces canonical finding identity, labels, and evidence. Matching must consider layer-specific identity as well as normalized file and line overlap. The shared scorer is pure and stable but may evolve through reviewed contract changes.

Ground truth is versioned independently from scanner code. Agents may locate candidates and propose annotations, but humans approve new or changed labels. Corrections require source evidence, rationale, review state, and a separate corpus delta so benchmark changes cannot be mistaken for scanner improvements.

Execution plan (parallel lanes, not a sequential waterfall):

Two parallel starting lanes:
- Evaluation lane: DATAP-c7dd46 (shared evaluator + component adapter)
- Corpus lane: DATAP-b17f92 (versioned ground-truth benchmark) — can start immediately alongside c7dd46 now that DATAP-9179d1 (curation skill/workflow) is complete

After shared evaluator contract stabilizes (c7dd46), these proceed in parallel:
- DATAP-d61496 (data-flow adapter)
- DATAP-f3feec (PII matcher and adapter)

Corpus supplies real cases to layer adapters once benchmark data exists, but benchmark work does not block starting the evaluator.

Sequential boundaries only:
- Layer adapters must not implement competing scorers before c7dd46 settles the shared contract
- Final benchmark serialization follows shared identity/evidence conventions from c7dd46
- Ground-truth labels require human approval before becoming accepted benchmark data

PII rule extraction is separated from any decision to expose new findings in default product output.

The experimental DATAP-602-BDD branch remains research input. Production work removes Cucumber and scratch artifacts while preserving useful pinned-repository provenance, adversarial cases, measured baselines, and unsupported-file handling.

comments.author: ryan
comments.text:
## Evaluation system plan — three-layer structure

Filed three child tasks for the planned PRs:

- DATAP-c7dd46 — Eval system: component detection (Layer 1, first PR, zero scanner changes)
- DATAP-d61496 — Eval system: data flow detection (Layer 2, follow-up, zero scanner changes)
- DATAP-f3feec — Eval system: PII signal matching (Layer 3, follow-up, minimal scanner change to un-gate PII regex)

### Shared design across all layers

The scoring engine is shared. Each layer has its own adapter (maps layer output → ReportedFinding[]) and case set. The scoring engine never changes — only the adapter and cases differ.

Three scores, never averaged:
- Recall: did we find it at all?
- Label accuracy: did we call it the right thing?
- Precision: did we avoid flagging things that are not sensitive?

### What we drop from the experimental branch (DATAP-602-BDD)

- Cucumber, Gherkin, .feature files
- hard-cases.ts (143 cases with research metadata — difficulty, technique, reason, taxonomy fields)
- precision-sample*.json (5 hand-labelled worksheets — research artifacts)
- population.ts, fixtures.ts (25 pinned external repos — no cloning)
- tmp/ scratch scripts
- All research-metadata fields from the data model
- The "BDD" label — this is a benchmark, not a living spec

### What we keep from the experimental branch

- The three-score design (recall, label, precision — never averaged)
- The "unread" concept for precision cases in unparsed files
- The location-based matching strategy (file/line overlap)
- The adversarial corpus philosophy (cases chosen because the scanner is expected to fail)
- The separation of curated scorecard from unbiased sampled measurement (the latter is future work)

### Key decision: decoupled from scanner

The eval system calls scan() with enableAiInference: false and reads existing public output. Zero src/ changes in the first PR. The adapter maps scanResult.components → ReportedFinding[]. When data-item detection lands in a future PR, a new adapter maps data items into the same ReportedFinding[] shape — the scoring engine doesn't change.

comments.author: ryan
comments.text:
## Revised evaluation plan supersedes the earlier three-layer comment

The prior comment remains as history, but its metric definitions and corpus-removal decisions are no longer authoritative.

Corrections now reflected in the epic and child descriptions:

- True precision requires exhaustively annotated scopes and counts unmatched scanner findings as false positives.
- Curated negative locations produce a negative-case pass rate, not precision.
- Label accuracy is conditional on matched positives; correct-label recall is reported separately.
- Exact scanned-file coverage determines unread status.
- Matching uses layer-specific identity plus normalized evidence, not location alone.
- Fast committed fixtures validate the harness; a pinned third-party benchmark measures scanner quality.
- Ground truth is human-approved, versioned, and corrected through explicit corpus deltas separate from scanner deltas.
- Data-flow evaluation resolves component IDs and uses deterministic flow type unless deterministic data categories are verified.
- PII rule matching is extracted as a pure deterministic function before any separate decision to change default product output.

New child tasks:

- DATAP-9179d1: repository selection and annotation workflow
- DATAP-b17f92: versioned ground-truth benchmark corpus

The reusable skill is named curate-scanner-evaluation-corpus.
